references.text: The psalmist describes how God stretches out the heavens like a tent and sets the beams of his chambers over the waters, a poetic reflection on the creation of the firmament (rakia) in Genesis 1:6.
The heavens declare God's glory, and the firmament (rakia - the same word as in Genesis 1:6) proclaims the work of his hands.
An invitation to praise God from the waters above the heavens, recalling the waters separated by the firmament in Genesis 1:6.
Job 37:18 uses the word rakia (firmament) and asks if Job can stretch out the heavens - a direct parallel to the creation of the firmament.
Isaiah describes God as stretching out the heavens like a curtain and spreading them out like a tent to dwell in, a reflection on the creation of the firmament.
Jeremiah describes God's creative power, including that he stretches out the heavens by his understanding - parallel to the creation of the firmament in Genesis 1:6.
Wisdom was present when God established the firmament over the deep and fixed the springs of the depths - a direct parallel to the separation of the waters.
Peter reminds us that from ancient times the heavens and earth were formed out of water and through water by God's word, reflecting the creation in Genesis 1:6.
Verse 20 shows how the firmament created in verse 6 serves as a framework for the next phase of creation.
Verse 14 elaborates on the function of the firmament separated in verse 6 by placing luminaries there.
It highlights God's sovereign power over water, which both creates order (Genesis) and makes salvation possible (Isaiah).
Psalm 19:2 interprets the firmament created in Genesis 1:6 as a testimony to God's glory.
